name: Aurelian

The ancients relate that Dijon was built by the Emperor Aurelian.

namesake_notes: Council of Orleans (Concil. Aurelian.), Aurelianus of Arles, Aurelianus envoy of Clovis, Caelius Aurelianus, Paul Aurelian of Brittany, Ambrosius Aurelianus, consul Aurelianus (400), Aurelianum = Orleans.
editorial_notes: Mommsen consular table, Acta Sanctorum footnote on Polycarp, Dalton/MGH notes, Samson of Dol introduction, Wasserschleben introduction.
comment: Visigothic S is Isidore's Chronicon entry (PL83, not the Historia section named in the shelf locus); Gregory's Dijon sentence (Dalton translation, text not note) is the only Merovingian S. Visigothic #1 is Victor/Jerome consular table in Mommsen, not Isidore/Biclaro section.

name: Priscillian

best_quote.text: Priscillianus, aceusan- te Itacio, a Maximo tyranno gladio czeditur
In consequence of which, in the year 384, Priscillian and many more were put to death.
Accordingly it is not Dictinius but Priscillian that they read

comment: Visigothic: three distinct Braga/Hispana anathemas (Manichaeus-substance, souls-cast-down, Sabellius-paraclete) counted once each across Bruns and collectio duplicates; two Isidore Chronicon entries; Isidore epitome "Priscillianus agnoscitur" counted once (Etymologiae and Mommsen apparatus-line 43135 are the same entry). Contexts 2 (Continuatio Chronicorum Hieronymianorum, line 1132) is not a shelved work, labelled U. Shakers: Testimony passages are the Ministry-authored text, partly quoting Robinson/Mosheim inside the work; counted S. Byzantine: Leo Ep. 15 to Turribius (NPNF translation); #5 and #6 are one paragraph (p67). Byzantine #1 and #3 are other works in the Mommsen file (Continuatio, Isidore), not the Victor section, so not S.

Syriac Orthodox S = Michael tome I (Phrygia prophetesses) and tome II (Montanus, Maximilla and Priscilla with gold plates, same Justinianic episode). Syriac renaissance shelves tome I only.

namesake_notes: none (Bardesanes is also used for the sage-name; Prisca-type confusions absent).
editorial_notes: Chabot and Abbeloos-Lamy footnotes, Nau table of contents/index (PO 8, PO 9), Hilgenfeld/Merx citations in the Persian martyr acts commentary, Parisot and Sachau introductions, Scher/Nau footnote on Bardesane death year.
comment: Please read per-context labels as follows. Syriac Orth: #0 and #6 Michael footnotes (E), #4 TOC (E), #9 Abbeloos-Lamy footnote on birth date (E); John of Ephesus #1/#2/#7/#8 are ONE passage (same text in two editions, one run of sentences) counted once. Church of East: #1 and #6 (Guidi Latin) fall in the Chronicon Miscellaneum, not the Khuzistan Chronicle the shelf names, so U not S. Persian early: Seert #4 and #7 are one passage; shelf has no Guidi.

name: Antony
namesake_notes: Overwhelmingly namesakes: Antony Fitzharberd, Antony Catisby, Sir Antony Browne, Sir Antony Cook, Antony Ager, Antony of Bourbon, Antony Froment, Antony Calvin, Antony de Mouvans, Antony Maillet and other personal names; Sainct Antony's in the Horsfare (York, a place/church); Antony's pit (Bristol, grave plot).
editorial_notes: Binney introduction list of parish stores (Morebath #0), Surtees Prymer editor note on a manuscript (#7), Hobhouse index line.
comment: No S. The Lynn gild ordinance (late-medieval #3), Morebath accounts "Sent Antony" (#4, #8 in Reformation; Morebath store) and the "Antony Crosse" at St Mary at Hill are very probably devotion to Anthony the Great, but the text never says which Anthony (Padua is possible), so U rather than S.

namesake_notes: Christiana = Latin/Spanish/Italian adjective "Christian" (doctrina Christiana, Res Christiana) throughout the Jesuit works; Christiana in Bunyan Pilgrim's Progress Part II is a fictional character; Trigault title and Calamy Latin are not the person.
editorial_notes: Georgian: Wardrop title-page metadata (#0), Armenian-version variant footnote (#4), running head (#9).
comment: Only the Georgian shelf has clean passages (7 distinct narrative passages from the Life of Nino translation). Jesuit and Old Dissent hits are all the word or a fictional namesake.

name: Basil

best_quote.text: qui, ut magnus Basilius dicit, antitypa sunt et oblata, ut Christi corpus et sanguis liant.
ἀλλὰ τὴν δεσποτικὴν. μόνην φωνὴν ἐπειπόντα, ἦν, δὴ καὶ Βασίλειος ὁ μέγας Εὺ- νομίῳ προήνεγχε
Thus the divine Basil observeth. Human souls Christ calleth a vineyard, about which He hath set as a hedge,

namesake_notes: Basil. / ed. Basil. = Basel (many hits in notes and elenchi); Basil of Seleucia (Isauria); the sebastos Basil (kyr Basileios) in the patriarchal acts; a nephew Basil of the patriarch (Historia patriarchica); the iconoclast-era Saint Basil in Nikodemos vol. 2; Basilius Kargaduris (Lambros).
editorial_notes: Migne notes citing Basel editions, Schaff footnote, Gass German introduction (Cabasilas), Thomas Smith Latin commentary in the Lucaris appendix.
comment: Byzantine reaches only 4. Several Basil hits sit outside the shelved locus: PG152 line 728 is Manuel Calecas (Dominican, Contra Graecos), not the patriarchal diplomata from line 81575 (U in Byzantine #4 and Hesychasm #2, #9); PO15 #7 is the Latin deputies cedula (other side). Mark of Ephesus Latin version in PO17 (#2) counted S as a translation of his Capita syllogistica. Kokkinos (Palamas PG151) lines 16355 and 16732 are two separate passages. Ottoman #0/#5 are one Mogila Confession citation in two Kimmel editions. Philokalia #3 (line 1989) author not pinned, shelved work text.

name: Vigilantius

best_quote.text: incidunt in damnatam haeresim Vigilantii hae¬ retici damnati, qui dixit ac dogmatizavit
They quote also Jerome against Vigilantius. "On this field" [in this matter], they say, "eleven hundred years ago, Jerome overcame Vigilantius."
Vigilantius, who would not have the Saints prayed to; and Jovinian, who put marriage on a level

namesake_notes: none; every hit is the Vigilantius opposed by Jerome.
editorial_notes: None counted as E. Not-S (U) hits are outside the shelved section: Mansi lines 112089-112339 sit in the Council of Sens 1528, not Lateran V or Pisa; Mirbt line 20468 is document 414 (Bellarmine), outside docs 307-333; Canisius marginal source references and a margin gloss (#1, #5) are printer/translator apparatus.
comment: Counts are conservative: Bullarium #0/#4/#7 is one continuous argument (one passage); Gerson #6/#9 are one reply (one passage) plus #2; Lutheran Apology passage appears in three editions (Bensow Swedish, Jacobs, Bente-Dau) = one passage, plus Olavus Petri. Gerson hits at lines ~64543-64686 are in a poverty tract in the same Du Pin volume, not one of the named schism treatises, counted S as Gerson own text. Latin papal could be argued up to 5 if each sentence were its own passage.

name: Geiseric

namesake_notes: none; all hits are Geiseric the Vandal king.
editorial_notes: Dalton translator notes and Arndt-Krusch footnotes on Gregory of Tours; Fredegar apparatus note (14th-c. hand); Halm word index to Victor of Vita (lines 8469, 9376); Gardner footnotes to the Dialogues (all six Roman hits).
comment: Latin Africa under Byzantium: hits #0,#2-#7 are Victor of Vita (Historia persecutionis, Vandal-era), which the shelf does not list for this file (only Corippus from line ~10546), and #1 is in Marcellinus Comes, not the Victor of Tunnuna section; all labelled U (not S) for that reason. If the coordinator shelves Victor of Vita they would be genuine S passages (about 6 distinct). Merovingian S = Gennadius chs. 78 and the Prosper entry, NPNF translation.

name: Sabas
namesake_notes: Sabbas = the envoy Sabbas, kellar of the Chudov monastery, sent by the tsar in 1666 (Ligarides history; all ten hits); "couvent de saint Sabbas" at Rome in the synaxary is a monastery named for the saint (place), not the person; Sabas I = a manuscript siglum.
editorial_notes: Palmer notes inside the Ligarides file, Basset/Bayan manuscript description (Sabas I).
comment: No S in any tradition. The Rome monastery of St Sabbas is named for him but the text does not mean the saint himself, so N under the brief.

editorial_notes: Caspari German notes on Martin of Braga (Vigilius letter to Profuturus), Migne/Arevalo notes in PL72 and PL80, Ewald-Hartmann regests, apparatus and indexes, Gardner notes/index, Mirbt names index (lines 34083, 38739).
comment: Visigothic has no S: Marcellinus Comes entries (#1, #6) are not the Isidore/Biclaro sections; PL80 #0 (Epistola IV, line 21501) lies outside the Sisebut/Braulio/Paulus works; #9 is an editorial note on Pyrrhus. Papal: Mansi line 4402 is under the running head Basel Council, not Florence (U); Gerson #1 lists "Vigilius primus" among popes of schisms (counted S, he is the only pope of that name) while #4 ("Vigilius vel Eugenius", 848) is unclear. Gregorian S = NPNF Gregory letters (Bk VII-ish letter on the Fifth Council; Bk IX letter on Aurelius) in translation.

name: Aidan

best_quote.text: They sent him a man called Aidan, a monk of great meekness and godliness, from the monastery of St Columba

namesake_notes: Welsh shelf: Aedan/Aidanus/Maidoc the disciple of St David (Rees Lives; Maedoc of Ferns); Aidan map Gabran, king of Dal Riata (Annales Cambriae and its editor notes).
editorial_notes: Tridentine: none counted as E; Roman Missal (England 1843) calendar line (#1) left U, an English calendar table whose wording is the translator's.
comment: Tridentine reaches 5 only if calendar and rubric mentions count: the clearly narrative S passages are 2 (martyrology entry 31 Aug, #2/#3; lesson on Oswald and Aidan, #5/#6); the other three are Bute's calendar line (#0) and two rubrics (#4 Vespers, #7 commemoration), which are the Breviary's own text but are not statements about him. Shelf locus names only Martyrology entries for 24/27 Oct, but the file is the whole Roman Breviary (Bute 1908), so treated as shelved.

Nikon replies #1 is Nikon's own reply quoting a gloss, while the shelf names Ligarides' answers there. Russian S = four distinct passages in Ligarides history; Palaiologan S = Plusiadenos (PG159, Greek/Latin) twice.

name: Gudit
namesake_notes: Every hit is Judith: the biblical heroine/book of Judith (Wyclif, Wycliffite Bible, Homilies, Latimer, Hooker, Dirk Philips, Hutterite chronicle, Zurich letters), or Anabaptist women named Judith. Only the alias Judith matched; Gudit, Yodit, Esato do not appear in these contexts.
editorial_notes: Forshall-Madden preface/glossary and Vaughan introduction mention Judith as a translated book.
comment: No S anywhere; the Ethiopian queen (Gudit) is not named in any later-tradition shelf text here.

name: Gerard
namesake_notes: Father John Gerard S.J. (Gunpowder Plot narrative, Morris), Miles Gerard priest-martyr, Theodoric Gerard S.J. (Ignatius letters, Salmeron), Gerard Groote, Gerard Zerbolt of Zutphen, "Gerard's goods" (Ignatius), Gerard in Chalcedon catalogue references.
editorial_notes: Thwaites footnote 3 to Jesuit Relations vol. 11 (Knights Hospitallers, "one Gerard", d. 1118) is the only mention of the Hospitaller Gerard; it is an editor's note (E), not the Jesuit text.
comment: No S. The only context about the right Gerard (Hospitaller, Jesuit Relations v11 line 10106) is editorial; Devotio Moderna hits are title lines and chapter headings for Gerard Groote.

name: Ewostatewos
namesake_notes: Only the alias Eustathius matched, always a different person: Eustathius of Thessalonica the grammarian (Bengel Gnomon), the martyr Eustathius Placidas (Paul of Aleppo), Eustathius of Antioch, Eustathius of Sebaste, a bishop of the Synod of Parthenia (Kimmel marginal).
editorial_notes: Kimmel marginal source citation "Eustathius Synod. Parthen." in the Jerusalem Synod acts (E, and a different Eustathius anyway).
comment: Ewostatewos of Sara'e (Ethiopian) is not named in any of these shelves.
